H. M. Consulate General,
Shanghai, 1060
31st, March, 1917.

My dear McEuen,

Many thanks for letting me see the
very interesting file about the Nielsens.
It would certainly appear that there is some
game afoot but it is rather difficult to say
what it might be.

I return the file herewith.

Yours sincerely,

（签名）

Cn/kno

K. J. McEuen, Esquire,
Captain Superintendent of Police,
Shanghai.

英国驻上海总领事馆，

1917年3月31日。

亲爱的 McEuen：

非常感谢让我查阅关于 Nielsen 一家的这份非常有趣的档案。
看来确实有些名堂，但很难说究竟是何意图。

现将档案随信退回。

此致，

（签名）

Cn/kno

K. J. McEuen 先生，
警务处处长，
上海。

Dear Sir:

At the suggestion of
Mr J J Kugan, I beg to submit
the following facts to you:

I am a courier carrying dis-
patches from the Ministry of Fo-
reign affairs in Petrograd to the
Russian Ambassador in Washing-
ton.

I am a British subject and
travel under a British passport
issued by the Consul General in
New York. I also have a
special Russian passport and
page_data.zh:

加拿大太平洋远洋服务有限公司
“俄罗斯皇后”号皇家邮船

1917年3月18日。

J. Burnside 巡官
上海警察厅。
上海。

尊敬的先生：

应 J J Kugan 先生的建议，谨向阁下呈报以下事实：

我是一名信使，负责将彼得格勒外交部发往华盛顿俄国大使的公文递送过去。

我是英国臣民，持纽约总领事签发的英国护照旅行。我还持有特殊的俄国护照以及

page_data.en:
2
commission (#57) as courier
from the Russian Government.
On the Transiberian train
leaving Petrograd Feb 7/20/17 I
had as fellow passenger a
youth who gave me his name
as C. Nielsen of Shanghai.
In chatting, I happened to
mention that I would sail
from Shanghai on the Empress
of Russia Mch 17, and that
my cabin, the only one I
could obtain in Petrograd was
#206 and that I hoped to get
the Local Agent in Shanghai to
change it for a better one when
I reached there.
Nielsen said: I can do better than
that for you; give me your ticket
and as Mr Shews, the local
agent is an intimate friend
of mine, I shall have him
change it for you and have
everything in readiness by the
time you get there."
(He was coming direct to
Shanghai whereas I was to
stay a few days in Pekin).
On my arrival in Shanghai
I was met by Nielsen who
calmly informed me that
he had handed in my ticket
by mistake to the gate keeper
at the Railroad Station in Shang-
hai when he arrived.
I accepted his explanation
but after meeting Mr Regan
and Mr Coleman of Gaston
Williams & Wigmore, I learned
that Nielsen's reputation was
rather a bad one.
I had a close search made
at the R.R. Station by the Traffic
manager's assistant who re-
ported that no such ticket
page_data.zh:
2
俄国政府颁发的信使委任状（第57号）。
在2月7/20/17离开彼得格勒的西伯利亚列车上，
我有一位年轻乘客，他自称是
来自上海的 C. Nielsen。
闲聊中，我偶然提到我将于3月17日
从上海乘坐“俄罗斯皇后”号启航，
我在彼得格勒能订到的唯一舱位
是206号，我希望到达上海后
能让当地代理人为我换一个更好的舱位。
Nielsen 说：我可以为您做得比这更好；
把您的船票给我，因为当地代理人
Shews 先生是我的密友，
我会让他为您更换，并在您
抵达时准备好一切。”
（他将直接前往
上海，而我则要在
北京停留几天）。
抵达上海后，
Nielsen 前来接我，并
平静地告诉我，
他抵达上海火车站时，
误将我的船票交给了
检票员。
我接受了他的解释，但在会见
加斯顿、威廉斯与威格莫尔公司的 Regan 先生
和 Coleman 先生后，我得知
Nielsen 的名声相当不好。
我让铁路局客运经理助理
在火车站进行了仔细搜寻，他报告说
没有收到此类船票

page_data.en:
had been handed in.
Bear in mind that I am
carrying 4 packages of im-
portant dispatches.
Aside from the loss or theft of
the ticket, which compelled me
to pay the agent in Shanghai
another $225⁰⁰ gold. it strikes
me that the mere money in-
volved might not have been
the sole reason for the disa-
ppearance of my ticket. It is
quite possible that our enemies
may have had some object in
detaining me or my packages
or both, in Shanghai.
Be that as it may these are
the facts and if they are of any
service to you I shall be happy.
Yours truly,
Ed. M. Gourdau

My address:
2203 Pine St. New Orleans, La. U.S.A.
page_data.zh:
被上交。
请记住，我携带着
4包重要公文。
除了船票丢失或被盗迫使我
向上海代理人再支付225.00金元外，
在我看来，仅涉及的金钱可能并非
船票失踪的唯一原因。
很有可能是我们的敌人
企图在上海扣留我或我的公文包，
或两者兼有。
无论如何，这些就是事实，
如果它们对您有任何用处，我将不胜荣幸。
此致，
Ed. M. Gourdau

我的地址：
美国路易斯安那州新奥尔良市松树街2203号。

March 28th, 1917.
REPORT ON C.Nielsen.
Made by D.I.Burnside. Forwarded by Chief Detective Inspector.
Sir,
I beg to forward herewith a letter received to-day from E.M.Gueydan giving information re Mr C.Nielsen, son of Gordius Nielsen.
Apparently when Gueydan arrived in Shanghai, Nielsen met him and told him that all rooms were engaged in the Astor House & Palace Hotel's, but that he would find good accomodation at Tollefsen's Private Hotel to which place Nielsen took him. Gueydan then called on Mr J.J.Kegan on a business matter at the Astor House who immediately had the four dispatch boxes removed to Messrs Gaston, Williams & Wigmore's strong room & advised Gueydan to stay with Mr Coleman at his private house. Later in the day Mr Kegan took Mr A.P.Blunt of H.B.M.Consulate to inspect the boxes and eventually told Gueydan to make a report of the loss of his passage ticket to the Consulate which was done resulting in the Authorities holding back Gueydan's passport & papers.
What I have heard regarding C.Nielsen is as follows:-
Towards the end of 1916, C.Nielsen applied to the firm of Messrs Gaston, Williams & Wigmore for employment stating that he was then employed with Seth Seth & Coy but wished to better himself. The firm gave Nielsen employment on a very small salary & shortly afterwards, began to get suspicious of his doings in the office on account of his enquiring into the firms private business matters, & overlooking the various typists doing confidential work which in no way concerned him. They then occupied his time running bogus errands in order to keep

关于 C. Nielsen 的报告。
由 D.I. Burnside 制作。由首席侦探督察转呈。
长官，
谨随函转呈今日收到的 E.M. Gueydan 来信，信中提供了关于 Gordius Nielsen 之子 C. Nielsen 先生的信息。
显然，当 Gueydan 抵达上海时，Nielsen 迎接了他，并告诉他礼查饭店（Astor House）和汇中饭店（Palace Hotel）的房间已全部订满，但他会在托勒夫森私人旅馆（Tollefsen's Private Hotel）找到良好的住宿，Nielsen 便将他带往该处。随后，Gueydan 因公务在礼查饭店拜访了 J.J. Kegan 先生，后者立即将四个公文箱移至加斯顿、威廉斯与威格莫尔公司的保险库，并建议 Gueydan 住在 Coleman 先生的私宅。当天晚些时候，Kegan 先生陪同英国驻华公使馆的 A.P. Blunt 先生检查了箱子，并最终建议 Gueydan 向领事馆报告船票遗失一事，Gueydan 照办，导致当局扣留了 Gueydan 的护照和文件。
我所听到的关于 C. Nielsen 的情况如下：
1916年底，C. Nielsen 向加斯顿、威廉斯与威格莫尔公司申请工作，声称当时受雇于 Seth Seth & Coy 公司，但希望改善处境。该公司以很低的薪水雇佣了 Nielsen，但不久后，开始怀疑他在办公室的行为，因为他打听公司的私人业务事项，并窥视从事机密工作的各类打字员，而这些与他毫无关系。于是他们让他去跑一些虚假的差事，以便让他

him out of the office and quietly commenced enquiries with the
result that they then found he had been formerly employed with
the Standard Oil Coy & had specially left this firm to join
Seth Seth & Coy in order to carry out his fathers wishes of
obtaining employment with Gaston, Williams & Wigmore.
    Whilst these enquiries were going on, C.Nielsen on Chinese
New Years day (23.1.17) entered the office, but on seeing
foreign employees were present, left immediately.    Messrs
Gaston, Williams & Wigmore make it a rule not to employ anyone
ever connected with the Standard Oil Coy, & fearing to openly
dismiss Nielsen, on account of the father's love for Courts &
writing to newspapers, quietly told C.Nielsen that they were
lessening the staff & his services were dispensed with.
    It was then that a former houseboy of H.O'Shea named Ting
Shou Shiang (丁訓相) applied for employment as a typist but
when put to the test, knew nothing as regards typing.    This
man was followed & found to visit the home of Gordius Nielsen &
to enter the back door of the Remington Typewriter Coy.
    A few days later, a young man giving the name of Hampton,&
who appeared to be a Eurasian or a native of Cairo, called at
the office of Gaston, Williams & Wigmore & enquired whether the
firm would be willing to do leather business.    This man was
asked for references but could not give any.    On account of
the firm doing a very extensive business in leather with the
Russian Government, they became suspicious of Hampton, & having
him followed, found that he visited the German Club & German

离开办公室，并悄悄开始调查，
结果发现他此前曾受雇于
美孚石油公司（Standard Oil Coy），并特意离开该公司加入
Seth Seth & Coy 公司，以实现其父亲
进入加斯顿、威廉斯与威格莫尔公司工作的愿望。
在进行这些调查期间，C. Nielsen 于中国
新年当天（1917年1月23日）进入办公室，但看到
有外籍员工在场，便立即离开。加斯顿、威廉斯与威格莫尔
公司有一条规定，永不雇佣任何与
美孚石油公司有关联的人，由于担心因其父亲
热衷诉讼和给报纸写信而不敢公开解雇 Nielsen，
便悄悄告诉 C. Nielsen 他们正在缩减人员，
不再需要他的服务。
就在那时，H. O'Shea 的前任男仆 Ting
Shou Shiang（丁训相）申请担任打字员，但
经过测试，他对打字一无所知。此人
被跟踪，发现他走访了 Gordius Nielsen 的住所，
并进入了雷明顿打字机公司（Remington Typewriter Coy）的后门。
几天后，一个自称 Hampton 的年轻人，
看起来像是欧亚混血儿或开罗人，来到
加斯顿、威廉斯与威格莫尔公司的办公室，询问
该公司是否愿意做皮革生意。此人
被要求提供推荐人，但无法提供。由于
该公司与俄国政府有着广泛的皮革业务往来，
他们对 Hampton 产生了怀疑，并派人跟踪，
发现他走访了德国总会和德国

Consulate.
The firm now strongly suspected that Nielsen's son, Ting
Shou Shiang & Hampton were endeavouring to obtain information,
most probably for Gordius Nielsen, to be conveyed to enemy
subjects.
Shortly after Nielsen left Gaston, Williams & Wigmore, the
firm began to receive anonymous letters regarding their employees
particularly a young man named Silar. Again this was put down
to Nielsen or his father, the young man Silar bearing the best
of characters.
In order to compare the notepaper of the anonymous letters
with that of Gordius Nielsen, the firm on a pretext, wrote to
Gordius Nielsen whose notepaper on reply was ~~to be~~ found to be
different. The letters were posted at the corner of Szechuen &
Canton Roads.
C.Nielsen left Shanghai about the middle of February last
via Siberia for his native place Denmark but for some reason or
other, was turned back at Petrograd. He is now said to be
about to take passage to America by the S.S. " Nippon Maru"
leaving on 29th inst:.
Your obedient servant.
J. Burnside.
Det: Inspᵗ
Chief Detective Inspector.

Shou Shiang 和 Hampton 正试图获取信息，
很可能是为 Gordius Nielsen 获取，以便传递给敌国
侨民。
Nielsen 离开加斯顿、威廉斯与威格莫尔公司后不久，
该公司开始收到关于其员工的匿名信，
特别是针对一位名叫 Silar 的年轻人。这再次被归咎于
Nielsen 或其父亲，尽管年轻人 Silar 品行端正。
为了将匿名信的信纸与 Gordius Nielsen 的信纸进行比对，
该公司找借口给 Gordius Nielsen 写了一封信，
发现回信的信纸 ~~是~~ 不同的。信件是从
四川路与广东路拐角处寄出的。
C. Nielsen 于去年二月中旬左右
经西伯利亚离开上海前往其祖国丹麦，但因某种原因，
在彼得格勒被遣返。据说他现在
准备乘坐本月29日启航的“日本丸”号轮船
前往美国。
您顺从的仆人。
J. Burnside.
